Augustus, Elector of Saxony.question: The _____ was Elector of Saxony from 1553 to 1586.
Augustus, Elector of Saxony.fact: Augustus (German: August; 31 July 1526 – 11 February 1586), who called himself Augustus and was popularly called "Father August" in reference to his paternal rule, was Elector of Saxony from 1553 until his death. Augustus, Elector of Saxony.subject: Courts Cases & Verdicts
Augustus, Elector of Saxony.question: Augustus ordered the leaders of the Crypto-_____ to be seized, and they were tortured and imprisoned
Augustus, Elector of Saxony.fact: The Crypto-Calvinists were confident that they would be able to bring Augustus over to their Calvinizing positions by convincing Augustus that they were in fact merely loyal Lutherans, when in fact they were working to introduce Calvinist views of the Lord's Supper, and the doctrine of predestination at the University of Wittenberg. Aulic Council.question: The _____ was One of the two supreme courts of the Holy Roman Empire (1498-1806).
Aulic Council.fact: The Aulic Council (Latin: Consilium Aulicum; German: Reichshofrat; literally 'Court Council of the Empire', sometimes abbreviated in academic writing as "RHR") was one of the two supreme courts of the Holy Roman Empire, the other being the Reichskammergericht (Imperial Chamber Court). Unlike the Reichskammergericht, which was tied to the Imperial estates, the Aulic Council was tied directly to the Emperor.

Aulic Council.subject: Courts Cases & Verdicts

Aulic Council.fact: Unlike the Reichskammergericht, which was tied to the Imperial estates, the Aulic Council was tied directly to the Emperor. It had not only concurrent jurisdiction with the Reichskammergericht, but in many cases exclusive jurisdiction: the Aulic Council had exclusive jurisdiction in all "feudal" processes, and in criminal affairs, over the immediate subjects of the Emperor and in affairs which concerned the Empire, and more (see Responsibilities section below).
